items.title: Zyxel GS1900 Patch Fails to Block Zero-Day Exploit Allowing Root Command Execution
items.summary: Zyxel GS1900 network switches that received the vendor's earlier fix for an actively exploited flaw are still open to the exploit attackers used, researchers at Binarly found. The exploit lets anyone who can reach a switch's web management interface run commands on it without log
items.author: Swati Khandelwal

items.title: Debian and Ubuntu APT Flaw Lets MitM Attackers Swap Verified Packages and Run Code as Root
items.summary: A flaw in APT, the package manager for Debian and Ubuntu, allows an attacker who can modify package downloads to swap a checked package for their own. The attacker's code then runs as root, according to advisories that Debian, Ubuntu, and APT's developers published on November 4.
items.author: Swati Khandelwal

items.title: APT29-Linked Hackers Hijack Web Analytics Script to Deliver iOS and Android Exploits
items.summary: The Russia-linked threat actor known as APT29 is presumed to be behind a large-scale watering hole campaign targeting iOS and Android users through compromised websites, fake domains, and a supply chain attack involving a Ukrainian web analytics service called Plerdy SEO Tracker.
items.author: Ravie Lakshmanan

items.summary: A critical flaw in Ruby on Rails could allow an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files on an app's server by uploading a crafted file if the app processes uploads using ImageMagick. The Rails project disclosed the flaw in an advisory and fixed it in versions 8.1.4.1 an
items.author: Swati Khandelwal

items.title: Xen Hypervisor Flaws Let One Malicious VM Read and Write Any Other VM's Memory
items.summary: Two flaws in the Xen hypervisor allow a malicious guest virtual machine (VM) to read and write the memory of other VMs on the same host, including dom0. Dom0 is the VM that, by default, has full permissions and manages the others. Patches are out, and there is no known mitigation
items.author: Swati Khandelwal

items.title: China-Aligned Hackers Hijack Sogou Input Method DNS Requests to Deploy DarkVigil Backdoor
items.summary: A China-aligned threat actor known as SlippyNunchucks has been attributed to a Domain Name System (DNS) hijacking operation abusing insecure HTTP communications in Windows versions of Sogou Input Method as part of a surveillance campaign designed to deploy an implant called DarkV
items.author: Ravie Lakshmanan

items.author: Swati Khandelwal
